architecture.transport_trust: Shared webhook token authenticates ingress. Payload instance must match configured instance. Receiver is supplied by server configuration, not webhook environment/module fields. This is not independent provider signature verification. Groups/LID are rejected until verified participant/receiver normalization exists.
architecture.environment: HTTP composition is still DEV-only; channel metadata must explicitly be dev. Dispatcher also checks channel/handler/identity environment. pro follows existing provider_credentials vocabulary; no PROD credentials or transport were enabled.
architecture.persistent_scope: Horizontal provider_instance storage key is horizontal-v1 plus an unambiguous JSON tuple of environment, provider, provider_id, physical instance, channel, workspace, tenant, module and receiver. Existing 026 unique indexes/queries/locks therefore scope threads, inbound deduplication, outbound intents, delivery and evidence. Physical instance stays in normalized message metadata. Legacy storage keys are unchanged. No new persistence migration is required for this scoped-key approach, but actual PG execution remains unvalidated.
architecture.identity: Read-only PhoneIdentityRepository expects proposed messaging_phone_bindings table and joins core_users; no table was created, no verification/enrollment procedure was invented. None means confirmed absent binding; invalid/revoked/ambiguous bindings raise InvalidIdentityBinding; DB errors never grant anonymous access.
architecture.permissions: Reuses PermissionConsoleRepository.list_effective_permissions for the bound active user/workspace. Trusted handler registration must declare a nonempty required_permissions gate in the HTTP builder. Module handlers must still authorize individual sensitive operations; no Telchi/Flow permission codes were invented.
architecture.public_policy: Defaults to none; public capabilities are explicit handler-registration declarations. Tests use Telchi denial and Flow public information doubles only; no real Flow public capabilities were approved or enabled.
architecture.legacy: Allowlist, ping, hola and fixed Telchi SQL preserved only in legacy DEV branch. Horizontal mode disallows legacy SQL tenant configuration and bypasses legacy processing.
architecture.delivery: Result and unique outbound intent commit atomically before sending. Atomic begin_send commits a sending fence before network I/O. Provider acceptance is not confirmed delivery; existing callbacks provide delivery/read status.
architecture.recovery: Duplicate inbound can resume an unsent durable intent without re-running the handler. Known transport failures require explicit retry=True through service API; no new unauthenticated retry endpoint exists. Sending/unknown outcomes and claim-without-result remain execution-uncertain and require reconciliation. A crash between claim and result commit is deliberately NOT auto-replayed. Recovery uses persisted destination and rejects changed senders. No broker or universal jobs framework.
architecture.exactly_once_limit: At-most-once handler invocation fence per durable inbound, not universal exactly-once business execution. No transactional coupling with module side effects or provider idempotency guarantee. Crash after send-start or provider acceptance may remain uncertain; no blind resend. No scheduled recovery worker was added. Legacy recovery gap is not claimed closed.
